ranking.note: Prerequisite for #29409 and the whole Chain-over-IPC chain; fixes crashes external callers can trigger, so it should be reviewed before the PRs stacked on it.
Raised to P1: it is the direct prerequisite of #10102/#19460 (both P1/P2 here) and a PR that unblocks several others cannot sit below them.
Still category-defining, but placed after the fixes and interface work it is stacked on, which reviewers must clear first.
Moved up: it is the only PR here fixing a concrete user-visible failure today (wrapper subcommands broken on distros with custom install dirs, issue #35785).

inconsistencies: Dependency chain whose review order matters: #36520 -> #29409 -> #10102 -> #19460 -> #19461. Each later PR is stacked on the earlier ones; reviewing them out of order wastes effort.

#35932 and #36572 both address crashes/races in IPC connection and event-loop teardown. #35932 covers the documented Antithesis crash reports (#35845, #33387) and should be reviewed first; #36572 should be checked for overlap with it and with the libmultiprocess teardown fixes #35932 pulls in.

#32387 (Windows IPC support, including the wrapper awaiting child processes) and #36190 (test for Windows wrapper child exit status, follow-up to merged #36105) touch the same Windows wrapper behaviour; review #32387 first so the test matches the final semantics.

#36097 (replaces mining interrupt methods with cancellation arguments on waitTipChanged/createNewBlock/waitNext) and #33922 (adds getMemoryLoad and template lifetime tracking) both modify the Mining IPC interface and its generated capnp definitions; they will conflict, and #36097 settles the call-shape question so it should land first.
#36097 and #35932 both carry temporary libmultiprocess subtree commits pending upstream PRs; the subtree sync should be coordinated rather than duplicated.
result.notes: The band spread is driven by the category's stated priorities: crash/correctness across the process boundary and the chain enabling wallet/GUI separation are P1; platform coverage, the mining test client, cancellation mechanics and the wrapper install fix are durable P2 work; test-coverage, flakiness and argument-parsing polish are P3. No P4 was needed: every PR here has an identified consumer or a reported issue behind it.
